security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU TCG, when translating a 16-bit compressed load/store instruction (C.LD/C.SD/C.LDSP/C.SDSP), the translator selects the wrong expansion path based on XLEN or misa bits: on RV32 with Zilsd enabled, the instruction must load/store a 64-bit value to/from a register pair (rd', rd'+1) using two 32-bit memory accesses, but if QEMU instead expands it as an RV64C single 64-bit register load/store (or vice versa on RV64), the emulated register state silently diverges from architectural expectations
security_spec.summary: Zilsd (RV32) and RV64C share identical compressed opcode encodings for C.LD/C.SD/C.LDSP/C.SDSP but with divergent semantics (register-pair vs single xreg); QEMU TCG must dispatch based on XLEN+misa.Zilsd or silently corrupt guest register state

findings.finding: Decode pattern interleaving between standard C instructions and Zclsd: on RV32 with Zclsd + F enabled (without RVC), the c_flw entry in the { } multi-pattern block matches the C.LD opcode (011 in Q0) before zclsd_ld is reached. trans_c_flw succeeds via REQUIRE_ZCF_OR_FC when F is present, causing the translator to execute a 32-bit FP load with wrong immediate decoding (uimm_cl_w instead of uimm_cl_d) instead of the Zclsd 64-bit register-pair load. The validation at tcg-cpu.c:850-861 only blocks RVC+RVF and explicit Zcf, not the Zca+RVF combination where Zca is implied by Zclsd.

Same decode interleaving issue for C.LDSP: on RV32 with Zclsd + F (no RVC), the c_flw entry at @c_lwsp format matches the C.LDSP opcode (011 in Q2) before zclsd_ldsp is reached, causing an FP load instead of a 64-bit register-pair load with wrong immediate decoding.

Decode interleaving for C.SD (Q0) and C.SDSP (Q2): on RV32 with Zclsd + F (no RVC), c_fsw can match before zclsd_sd, causing an FP store instead of a 64-bit register-pair store. This applies to both Q0 @cs_d (lines 136-141) and Q2 @c_sdsp (lines 222-227).

Validation gap: Zclsd+RVC+F and Zclsd+Zcf are correctly blocked, but Zclsd+Zca+F (where Zca is implied by Zclsd) is not explicitly forbidden. Zclsd auto-enables Zca (line 1135), and F can be independently enabled. In this configuration, c_flw/c_fsw become valid 16-bit instructions that share opcodes with Zclsd's C.LD/C.SD — and since they appear before zclsd_* in the decode blocks, they win the pattern match, silently producing wrong instruction semantics.

Correctly implements Zilsd/Zclsd 64-bit load semantics on RV32: uses a single 64-bit qemu_ld_i64 (MO_SQ) for atomicity, extracts high/low halves via tcg_gen_extr_i64_tl, writes to register pair (rd, rd+1). Rejects odd-numbered rd (unaligned register pair). rd=0 special case correctly performs the load (for side effects) but skips register writes.

Correctly implements Zilsd/Zclsd 64-bit store semantics on RV32: concatenates register pair (rs2, rs2+1) via tcg_gen_concat_tl_i64, performs single 64-bit qemu_st_i64 (MO_SQ). Rejects odd-numbered rs2. rs2=0 special case correctly stores zero.
findings.snippet:
tcg_gen_concat_tl_i64(tmp, data_low, data_high);
tcg_gen_qemu_st_i64(tmp, addr, ctx->mem_idx, MO_SQ | mo_endian(ctx));

findings.finding: All Zilsd/Zclsd translator entry points correctly gate on REQUIRE_32BIT, preventing these functions from executing on RV64 or RV128 where single-register LD/SD should be used instead. The Zilsd variants check ext_zilsd; the Zclsd variants check ext_zclsd. trans_zclsd_ldsp additionally rejects rd=0 (per spec RES).

The 32-bit encoded LD/SD opcodes also use { } overlapping patterns (trans_ld vs zilsd_ld, trans_sd vs zilsd_sd). Unlike the 16-bit case, there is no intermediate pattern (no c_flw equivalent) between them, so the decode priority is a clean two-entry choice: RV64 path first, RV32+Zilsd second. Safe as designed.
